paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus can do what nobody else in that crowd could do, and He meets us right where our faith runs thin. The dad said, "But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us." Jesus echoed, "If You can?" and then said, "All things are possible to him who believes!" (Mark 9:22-23). That one sentence is about who Jesus is, not about how strong the dad's faith was.

Now look at what the dad does next. He doesn't clean up his answer or fake a big confident speech. He cries out, "I do believe; help my unbelief!" (Mark 9:24). I think that's the most honest prayer a person can pray, and the passage shows Jesus step in right after it. So bring Him the mixed-up, half-sure, wobbly version of your faith, friend, because that's the version He's asking for.

The disciples ask Jesus privately why they couldn't drive the spirit out, and He answers, "This kind cannot come out, except by prayer" (Mark 9:28-29). Prayer is how we lean on Him instead of leaning on ourselves. I'm a stamper who spent years in the back of a drawer, and I can tell you that leaning on yourself runs out FAST. Keep praying, keep bringing your needs to Jesus, and trust that He can do what you can't.
